claims.text: Controlled annealing induces local or short-range atomic ordering in the as-cast high-entropy alloy.
Annealing-induced local atomic ordering enhances electron–phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron–phonon coupling promotes a clearer superconducting transition at low temperature.
The selected as-cast alloy has significant chemical and structural disorder.
The selected as-cast alloy has weak or absent superconductivity.
The proposed effect occurs below approximately 10 K at ambient pressure.
The proposed effect requires the alloy to retain a uniform crystalline phase.
Annealing produces a more homogeneous or locally ordered atomic arrangement within a single-phase crystalline matrix.
Annealing reduces chemical inhomogeneities and local structural variations.
Reduced chemical and structural inhomogeneity sharpens specific lattice vibrational modes.
Sharpened lattice vibrational modes enhance electron–phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron–phonon coupling facilitates Cooper-pair formation in the alloy.
Annealed samples will exhibit a sharper superconducting transition than the as-cast samples.
Annealed samples may exhibit a higher critical temperature than the as-cast samples.
The as-cast baseline has a heterogeneous or multiphase structure.
The beneficial effect is limited to moderate annealing that avoids excessive grain growth and phase separation.
Excessive grain growth or phase separation removes the beneficial effect on electron–phonon coupling.
The magnitude of the critical-temperature improvement depends on the annealing parameters.
X-ray diffraction and EDXS can assess crystalline phase and compositional uniformity, respectively.
Electrical resistivity and magnetic susceptibility can jointly identify a superconducting transition and bulk diamagnetic response.

contradictions.description: The test conditions require a uniform crystalline phase, whereas the stated as-cast baseline is heterogeneous or multiphasic; it is unclear how both baseline and annealed samples can be tested under the same phase condition.
The initial state allows superconductivity to be absent, but the predicted comparison calls for a sharper or higher Tc; transition sharpness and Tc are undefined for a baseline with no transition.
